statement.text:
Simplest model of gas discharge
An external ionizer creates \(Z_{ext}\) electron and singly charged ion pairs per unit volume per unit time. Recombination removes pairs at rate \(rn_en_i\), where \(r\) is constant. Initially both densities are zero. In part A ignore the electric field of the carriers. For current measurements a gas-filled tube has parallel electrodes of area \(S\), separation \(L\ll\sqrt S\), and voltage \(U\). Both carrier species have drift-speed magnitude \(v=\beta E\), and their densities are approximated as uniform.
A1. Density growth constants
Write \(n_e(t)=n_0+a\tanh(bt)\). Determine \(n_0,a,b\).
A2. Two ionizers
Two ionizers separately produce equilibrium electron densities \(12\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}\) and \(16\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}\). Find the density with both operating.
A3. Current-voltage law
With the ionizer operating for a long time, express total current in terms of \(U,\beta,L,S,Z_{ext},r,e\).
A4. Low-voltage resistivity
Find gas resistivity at sufficiently small voltage.
B1. Electron current constants

For part B neglect recombination, keep \(Z_{ext}\), and take uniform field. The cathode is at \(x=0\), anode at \(x=L\). Avalanches obey \(dN_e/dl=\alpha N_e\). Write \(I_e(x)=C_1e^{A_1x}+A_2\) and find \(A_1,A_2\).
B2. Ion current constants
Write \(I_i(x)=C_2+B_1e^{B_2x}\). Find \(B_1,B_2\).
B3. Anode boundary
State the ion-current boundary condition at the anode.
B4. Cathode boundary
Each ion striking the cathode releases on average \(\gamma\) electrons. State the boundary condition at \(x=0\).
B5. Finite total current
Find the total steady current while the subcritical solution remains finite.
B6. Critical gap length
Find the gap length above which secondary emission can maintain discharge without the external ionizer.

children.text: Pairs are created and destroyed together, so \(n_e=n_i=n\) and \(\dot n=Z_{ext}-rn^2\). The initial condition and substitution give \[n_0=0,\quad a=\sqrt{Z_{ext}/r},\quad b=\sqrt{rZ_{ext}}.\]
Rates add, not equilibrium densities. Thus \(n=\sqrt{n_1^2+n_2^2}=20\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}\).

Each carrier current is \(I/2=en\beta US/L\). Pair balance is \(Z_{ext}SL=rn^2SL+I/(2e)\). The positive quadratic root gives \[I=\frac{e\beta^2U^2S}{rL^3}\left(\sqrt{1+\frac{4rZ_{ext}L^4}{\beta^2U^2}}-1\right).\]
Ion production gives \(-dI_i/dx=eZ_{ext}S+\alpha I_e\). Therefore \(B_1=-C_1\) and \(B_2=\alpha\).
No ions enter from beyond the anode, so \(I_i(L)=0\).

Total current \(I=I_e+I_i=C_2-eZ_{ext}S/\alpha\) is independent of position. Use \(C_2=C_1e^{\alpha L}\) and the cathode condition to obtain \[I=\frac{eZ_{ext}S}{\alpha}\left[\frac1{(1+\gamma)e^{-\alpha L}-\gamma}-1\right].\] The physical externally sustained branch has \(\gamma(e^{\alpha L}-1)<1\).

The avalanche feedback threshold is \(\gamma(e^{\alpha L}-1)=1\). Thus \[L_{cr}=\frac1\alpha\ln(1+1/\gamma).\] The linear model diverges at threshold and cannot predict the saturated discharge current.

solution.text:
Simplest model of gas discharge
A1. Density growth constants
Pairs are created and destroyed together, so \(n_e=n_i=n\) and \(\dot n=Z_{ext}-rn^2\). The initial condition and substitution give \[n_0=0,\quad a=\sqrt{Z_{ext}/r},\quad b=\sqrt{rZ_{ext}}.\]
A2. Two ionizers
Rates add, not equilibrium densities. Thus \(n=\sqrt{n_1^2+n_2^2}=20\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}\).
A3. Current-voltage law
Each carrier current is \(I/2=en\beta US/L\). Pair balance is \(Z_{ext}SL=rn^2SL+I/(2e)\). The positive quadratic root gives \[I=\frac{e\beta^2U^2S}{rL^3}\left(\sqrt{1+\frac{4rZ_{ext}L^4}{\beta^2U^2}}-1\right).\]
A4. Low-voltage resistivity
As \(U\to0\), \(n\to\sqrt{Z_{ext}/r}\) and \(I=2e\beta US\sqrt{Z_{ext}/r}/L\). Hence \[\rho_{gas}=\frac1{2e\beta}\sqrt{r/Z_{ext}}.\]
B1. Electron current constants
Local balance gives \(dI_e/dx=eZ_{ext}S+\alpha I_e\), so \(A_1=\alpha\), \(A_2=-eZ_{ext}S/\alpha\).
B2. Ion current constants
Ion production gives \(-dI_i/dx=eZ_{ext}S+\alpha I_e\). Therefore \(B_1=-C_1\) and \(B_2=\alpha\).
B3. Anode boundary
No ions enter from beyond the anode, so \(I_i(L)=0\).
B4. Cathode boundary
The secondary-emission condition is \(I_e(0)=\gamma I_i(0)\).
B5. Finite total current
Total current \(I=I_e+I_i=C_2-eZ_{ext}S/\alpha\) is independent of position. Use \(C_2=C_1e^{\alpha L}\) and the cathode condition to obtain \[I=\frac{eZ_{ext}S}{\alpha}\left[\frac1{(1+\gamma)e^{-\alpha L}-\gamma}-1\right].\] The physical externally sustained branch has \(\gamma(e^{\alpha L}-1)<1\).
B6. Critical gap length
The avalanche feedback threshold is \(\gamma(e^{\alpha L}-1)=1\). Thus \[L_{cr}=\frac1\alpha\ln(1+1/\gamma).\] The linear model diverges at threshold and cannot predict the saturated discharge current.
